meta.subtitle: Multiplayer pirate strategy game — Supabase edge-function server, deterministic TS engine, React/Pixi web client
meta.commit: main @ 5750da3 (fix verification); findings originally filed against dev @ 4ca6782 and prior commits
meta.authModel: Supabase Auth via OAuth (Google/GitHub) + anonymous play — service-role edge functions are the authoritative game-state boundary, not client-trusted RLS alone.
meta.headline: A full-repo audit (engine, server, client, cross-cutting) surfaced 1 critical and 11 high-severity issues — including two exploitable anti-cheat holes, an RLS self-recursion bug, an unauthenticated payments webhook path, and a dead-end OAuth flow. All 54 findings were filed as GitHub issues (AoP #205–256) and every one was independently re-verified against current main by re-reading the fixed source, not by trusting issue-closed status. 53 of 54 are fully fixed; 1 (asset hygiene) is partially fixed with two operator-flagged sub-items still open.
meta.scope: Full monorepo: packages/engine (deterministic game logic), packages/shared, packages/content, supabase/functions (edge-function server tier) and supabase/migrations (RLS/schema), apps/web (client), CI/CD workflows, and repository hygiene (asset size, docs accuracy). Plus a schema-level PII/data-classification scan.
meta.methodology: Three parallel static-review passes (engine / server / client) plus a cross-cutting principal-architect pass, together producing 54 findings filed as individual GitHub issues. Every finding was independently re-verified post-fix against current main by an agent re-reading the actual current source at the cited file/line — not inferred from the issue being closed — specifically because an earlier squash-merge (AoP #280) was found to have silently dropped several fixes from landing on main. PII scan via tools/pii-classify.mjs (name-based column classifier) statically parsed against all 23 migration files.
meta.outOfScope: Live dynamic penetration testing (M2) and Supabase performance/security advisors (M7) — deferred. The connected Supabase project's public schema is currently empty (unmigrated), so live-DB-dependent modules would find nothing meaningful today; re-run once the project is migrated with representative data.

findings.title: Client-submittable gainCaptainXp action grants arbitrary XP
findings.evidence: Action was in the public union with only an amount<=0 guard in the reducer; no production caller, but any client could submit amount:1e9 over the wire.
findings.impact: Any client could max out captain XP/skills on its turn — accepted, logged, and replayed cleanly, making it undetectable cheating under the server-authoritative model.
findings.fix: assertClientSubmittable() added in the server-side action gate (match.ts:403), rejecting gainCaptainXp from client submission outright; wired into submit-action/appendAction.

findings.title: Numeric action fields accepted NaN/fractional/oversized values
findings.evidence: recruit.count, transferTroops.count, gainCaptainXp.amount, and moveCaptain coordinates had no Number.isInteger-style guard — fractional/oversized values passed all engine checks.
findings.impact: Fractional recruit/transfer counts could corrupt integer-pool assumptions in GameState; oversized values were fully exploitable over the wire.
findings.fix: Shared reqInt() (Number.isSafeInteger) validator applied to every numeric action field at the submit-action boundary, ahead of the engine reducer.

findings.title: Self-referencing RLS policy on match_players caused Postgres infinite recursion
findings.evidence: match_players_select_own_matches subqueried match_players from within its own policy — Postgres raises infinite-recursion-in-policy at plan time, poisoning reads across matches/chat/actions/spectators/profiles.
findings.impact: Every authenticated client read of the game tables (outside edge functions, which use the service role) would fail.
findings.fix: SECURITY DEFINER helper user_match_ids() added; match_players_select_own_matches, matches_select_seated, and profiles_select_co_participants rewritten to call it instead of self-querying.

findings.title: stripe-webhook and compact-snapshots had no verify_jwt=false override
findings.evidence: No config.toml override or deploy flag anywhere in the repo — hosted default JWT verification would 401 Stripe's un-authenticated webhook and the cron's CRON_SECRET bearer.
findings.impact: Payments could be charged with entitlement never granted (silent revenue/trust failure); scheduled snapshot compaction would never run.
findings.fix: verify_jwt = false set explicitly for [functions.stripe-webhook] and [functions.compact-snapshots] in config.toml.

findings.title: Matchmaking accepted match_size 6-8 with only 5 factions defined
findings.evidence: FACTION_IDS has 5 entries but the match_size check constraint allowed 2-8; groups of 6-8 were drained (queue rows deleted) then assignQuickMatchSeats threw, stranding those players with no compensation.
findings.impact: 6-8 player queue groups were silently discarded after their queue entries were already deleted — players stranded with no feedback, and the drain aborted other buckets sharing the sweep.
findings.fix: match_size constraint capped at FACTION_IDS.length (5) at both the DB constraint and parseSettings; restoreQueueGroup() re-queues a group via upsert on any downstream createQuickMatch failure instead of losing it.

findings.title: Stripe checkout had no idempotency key or already-owned/payment-status check
findings.evidence: No Stripe Idempotency-Key on session creation; webhook granted remove_ads on any completed session regardless of payment_status or product.
findings.impact: Double-charge risk on retried checkout creation; a duplicate or wrong-product webhook event could grant entitlements incorrectly (duplicate delivery itself was already idempotent via upsert).
findings.fix: Idempotency-Key added to session creation; create-checkout-session now checks for an existing entitlement first; webhook only grants when payment_status==='paid' and metadata.product matches the expected SKU.

findings.title: Match actions persisted verbatim with no size or shape cap
findings.evidence: Client action objects were spread directly into storage with no whitelist or size limit — arbitrary junk fields could ride the action log forever, re-parsed on every state reconstruction and served in replays.
findings.impact: Unbounded per-action payload size is a storage-cost and replay-integrity risk, and a vector for junk/malicious fields to persist indefinitely.
findings.fix: sanitizeAction() rebuilds each action from a fixed per-type field whitelist; a DB-level CHECK (octet_length(action::text) <= 32768) backstops it.

findings.title: Finished-match action logs were world-readable, including private matches
findings.evidence: The finished-match read policy had no participant scoping, inconsistent with the participant-gated match_seed() policy — anyone could read the full action log of any finished match, private or not.
findings.impact: Exposes full replay/action history of private matches to any authenticated (or anonymous) client.
findings.fix: match_actions_select_finished rewritten to require match_id IN (SELECT user_match_ids(auth.uid())) in addition to status='finished'.

findings.title: Realtime match:{id} channels were unauthenticated
findings.evidence: Clients could forge turn/chat pokes on any match's realtime channel and outsiders could observe activity timing, since channels had no auth gate.
findings.impact: Refetch-amplification via forged pokes, and unintended activity-timing leakage to non-participants.
findings.fix: RLS policy match_channel_receive added on realtime.messages (participant/spectator-gated, SELECT-only, no client INSERT policy); broadcasts now sent with config:{private:true}.

findings.title: OAuth sign-in was a dead end — redirect tokens never parsed
findings.evidence: No location.hash / access_token parsing anywhere in the client (the app avoids supabase-js) — completing a Google/GitHub OAuth flow left the user signed out with tokens exposed in the URL.
findings.impact: Every OAuth sign-in attempt failed silently from the user's perspective, and access/refresh tokens briefly sat exposed in the URL bar/history.
findings.fix: Boot-time parseOAuthCallbackHash(window.location.hash) added, storing the session and clearing the URL fragment via history.replaceState.

findings.title: Access token never refreshed after mount — authed features died after ~1 hour
findings.evidence: Only a mount-time isExpired check existed; long-lived clients captured a frozen session and every authed call silently 401'd once the token expired.
findings.impact: QuickMatch polling and Spectate would silently stall ('Searching…' forever / frozen data) for any session older than ~1 hour with no user-facing error.
findings.fix: Single-flight getFreshSession() helper added with a 401-refresh-retry-once pattern, used by all authed calls.

findings.title: appendAction was two non-transactional statements
findings.evidence: insert(match_actions) and update(matches.action_count) were separate PostgREST calls; a crash between them permanently wedged the match — every later append hit a PK 23505 conflict forever, and reconstructState never saw the orphan row.
findings.impact: A single mid-request crash could permanently brick any in-progress match with no recovery path.
findings.fix: Replaced with a single SECURITY DEFINER RPC (append_match_action, one transaction) that also self-heals on 23505 conflicts.

findings.title: Quick-match drain had no compensation on downstream failure
findings.evidence: Claim-then-create had no rollback: a crash or downstream failure after a queue group's rows were deleted left those players silently unqueued with no re-entry.
findings.impact: Players could vanish from the matchmaking queue with no match and no notification, a support/trust problem at scale.
findings.fix: restoreQueueGroup() re-queues a claimed group via upsert on any createQuickMatch failure, and the drain no longer rethrows past a single poisoned bucket.

findings.title: join-match faction uniqueness was check-then-insert with no backing constraint
findings.evidence: Code comments claimed a DB uniqueness constraint on (match_id, faction) that did not exist — two concurrent joiners could race into the same faction.
findings.impact: Two players could end up seated as the same faction in one match, breaking downstream faction-keyed logic.
findings.fix: Unique index match_players_match_faction_key added on (match_id, faction), backstopping the existing 23505 handler.

findings.title: join-match could seat a player after start-match had already frozen the config
findings.evidence: A join landing between start-match's seat read and match activation created a DB seat row with no corresponding GameState seat — a permanently stuck NOT_YOUR_TURN player.
findings.impact: Affected players could join a match lobby and then be permanently unable to play, with no error surfaced.
findings.fix: sweepLateJoinSeats() deletes any seat >= the frozen seat count post-activation; called from both start-match and createQuickMatch.

findings.title: Cron/pg_net failures were invisible — job_run_details always reported success
findings.evidence: pg_net's fire-and-forget model meant HTTP-level failures in scheduled sweep/drain/compaction jobs never surfaced anywhere.
findings.impact: A cron job could fail silently and permanently with zero operator visibility — matches frozen at deadlines, queue growing unbounded.
findings.fix: maintenance_heartbeats table + a minute cron added that resolves net._http_response outcomes to ok/error/timed_out.

findings.title: sweep-turns processed every expired match serially with no limit
findings.evidence: One poisoned or slow match could starve every match sorted after it in the batch, indefinitely, since the sweep had no cap and no error isolation.
findings.impact: A single bad match record could stall turn-expiry processing for the entire game population.
findings.fix: MAX_EXPIRED_TURNS_PER_SWEEP=50 cap added; findExpiredTurns() processes oldest-first with a LIMIT.

findings.title: No retention policy for finished matches
findings.evidence: Snapshot compaction skipped non-active matches entirely; chat history for finished matches was unbounded (up to ~43K messages/seat/day theoretical).
findings.impact: Unbounded storage growth for a system with no natural archival path.
findings.fix: compact-snapshots now compacts finished-match snapshots to {seq 0, final} and calls purgeExpiredChat() with a retention window.

findings.title: Account deletion failed on FK constraints for anyone who ever played
findings.evidence: None of the three FKs had an ON DELETE behavior — deleting an auth.users row aborted for any user who had ever joined, created, or spectated a match.
findings.impact: No working account-deletion path existed for the majority of the user base (GDPR/compliance-relevant).
findings.fix: ON DELETE SET NULL migration applied to all three FKs, with a null-user convention documented for AI seats.

findings.title: No rate limit on create-match and no lobby expiry
findings.evidence: Lobbies never transitioned to 'abandoned' by anything, and match creation had no per-user rate limit — the match browser could be buried in spam lobbies.
findings.impact: Unbounded lobby accumulation degrades the match-browsing experience and offers a low-effort spam vector.
findings.fix: Per-user open-lobby rate limit added to create-match; hourly cron expires lobbies past a TTL.

findings.title: end-turn lacked the expectedSeq optimistic-concurrency token
findings.evidence: submit-action required an expectedSeq token to prevent stale writes; end-turn did not — a delayed duplicate request could silently end a fresh turn once the turn cycled back.
findings.impact: A retried/duplicated end-turn network request could end the wrong turn in 2-player-plus-AI matches.
findings.fix: end-turn now requires expectedSeq and calls the same assertExpectedSeq() check as submit-action.

findings.title: validateMapDefinition passed maps that crash createGame
findings.evidence: No check required a port tile on each home island; a validator-accepted community map could throw an unhandled Error the moment a match tried to start on it.
findings.impact: A published community map could pass validation, then 500 any attempt to start a match on it — unplayable map, no useful error to the author.
findings.fix: mapDefinition.ts now checks portCount===0/>1 per home island at validation time, matching what createGame actually requires.

findings.title: Resigned/eliminated players left zombie captains and cities in play
findings.evidence: eliminatePlayer didn't sweep the seat's captains/cities — ghost fleets remained farmable for XP, the AI wasted turns fighting dead seats, and dead cities kept replenishing recruit pools.
findings.impact: Free XP farming off ghost fleets and wasted AI compute fighting seats that had already resigned.
findings.fix: eliminatePlayer now filters out the eliminated seat's cities and releases its captives as part of the same reducer branch.

findings.title: Proportional casualty rounding could wipe a crew on sub-lethal damage
findings.evidence: Math.round(count*scale) could kill a full 1-unit stack at 60% damage (or spare it at lethal damage), flipping boarding eligibility unpredictably.
findings.impact: Deterministic but unfair combat outcomes at low troop counts, undermining trust in the combat resolution.
findings.fix: Casualties now tracked against a running total-health pool, matching the battle board's existing applyStackDamage approach.

findings.title: Author-placed land resource nodes could never yield
findings.evidence: Node-control required a water-only captain on the tile, but the editor/validator accepted land-placed resource nodes that could then never be controlled — plus an undocumented co-occupation tie-break.
findings.impact: Editor-placed land nodes silently never generated income, with no error to the map author.
findings.fix: An ownerSeat fallback lets unoccupied land nodes yield to their authored owner; the co-occupation tie-break is now documented.

findings.title: Attacker earned full combatWinXp even when the defender escaped
findings.evidence: Full XP was awarded regardless of whether the defender actually escaped, letting an attacker repeatedly bank full combat XP risk-free against an evading opponent.
findings.impact: A repeatable, risk-free XP farm against any AI or player that reliably evades.
findings.fix: combatWinXp is now zeroed when report.escapedId is set, instead of always awarding full value.

findings.title: isTestPlay flag never reset when loading a real save
findings.evidence: handleLoadSlot never reset isTestPlay, so loading a real save during test play left autosave silently disabled for it; 'Play Again' from test play inverted the flag and could autosave scratch data over a real slot.
findings.impact: Silent autosave loss for real save games under a specific but reachable navigation sequence.
findings.fix: setIsTestPlay() now explicitly reset by dedicated isTestPlayAfterLoadSlot()/isTestPlayAfterRematch() helpers on every load/rematch path.

findings.title: Save/load failures were swallowed everywhere
findings.evidence: Autosave errors (e.g. quota) were void; SaveScreen had no try/catch; load errors — including a deliberate newer-schema-version throw — closed the sheet with zero user-facing feedback.
findings.impact: A player could lose progress with no indication anything went wrong.
findings.fix: Autosave now sets an autosaveFailing state on failure; SaveScreen wraps save/load in try/catch and surfaces a status message.

findings.title: Map editor draft lived only in component state
findings.evidence: Test Play unmounted the editor, returning to a blank draft; Back had no confirmation guard — up to ten minutes of map editing could be silently destroyed.
findings.impact: Unrecoverable loss of in-progress map-editing work on a routine navigation action.
findings.fix: Debounced IndexedDB autosave of the working draft added, rehydrated on remount; Back and all destructive actions (New/Generate/Import) now go through a single guardedReplace() confirmation helper.

findings.title: Quick-match queue entries leaked on navigation
findings.evidence: Navigating away and back kept the client queued without the player's knowledge; the poll swallowed all errors forever, including permanent ones; the 'found' state could show an empty matchId with only a 'Back to Menu' escape.
findings.impact: Players could be silently seated into matches they never learned about, or get stuck in a dead-end queue screen.
findings.fix: client.leave() now runs in the screen's cleanup effect; permanent vs. transient poll errors are distinguished; the 'found' UI is gated on a non-null matchId.

findings.title: No ErrorBoundary; invalid AI actions permanently froze the game
findings.evidence: An InvalidActionError dispatched from setTimeout during an AI turn had no catch and no effect-dependency change to recover from — the game froze permanently on 'AI thinking…'; human invalid actions were silently dropped.
findings.impact: A single bad AI action could permanently soft-lock any match for all players in it.
findings.fix: Top-level React ErrorBoundary added; AI-dispatched action failures now force an end-turn/resign for that seat with a toast; human-invalid actions surface a toast instead of silently dropping.

findings.title: usePixiApp swallowed WebGL init failure
findings.evidence: Application.init() had no .catch — a WebGL failure produced a permanent blank map with no message to the player.
findings.impact: Players on WebGL-incompatible devices/browsers saw a blank screen with no explanation and no fallback.
findings.fix: init() failure now caught, exposed as an error state, with fallback UI and a canvas-preference fallback.

findings.title: Multiplayer client modules were fully unwired
findings.evidence: turnSync, reconnectSync, useMatchChat, ChatPanel, and DiplomacyPanel had zero non-test importers and no Realtime transport wired — every online multiplayer flow dead-ended before actual gameplay. This fix was one of the ones an earlier squash-merge (PR #262) dropped; recovered in a later batch (commit 5b7fee8, PR #290).
findings.impact: The entire online multiplayer feature was non-functional in the shipped client despite the server/engine support existing.
findings.fix: MatchScreen.tsx now imports and wires DiplomacyPanel, MatchChatPanel, browserResyncTransport, MatchActionClient, subscribeReconnectSync, and subscribeTurnSync; App.tsx routes to it.

findings.title: Stripe checkout return had no fulfillment handling
findings.evidence: successUrl and cancelUrl were identical with no marker; a single entitlement fetch raced the webhook and failed open, showing the buy button again — inviting a double purchase. Also dropped by PR #262's squash-merge, recovered in the same later batch as F-33.
findings.impact: Buyers landing back on the app immediately after a successful purchase could be shown the buy button again before the webhook granted their entitlement.
findings.fix: useRemoveAdsStatus() now exposes a purchasePending state; checkout.ts polls entitlement status with backoff instead of a single race-prone fetch.

findings.title: A* pathfinding was O(n) per step with a whole-ocean flood-fill fallback
findings.evidence: The A* open list was a linear scan, unreachable goals triggered a full-ocean flood-fill, and the AI recomputed all paths from scratch on every action — tens of full-ocean A* runs per AI turn on 8-seat maps.
findings.impact: Meaningfully slower browser AI turns and reduced balance-sim throughput on larger maps.
findings.fix: Binary heap open list (byte-identical (f,h,tileIndex) tie-break preserved), a cached water-component flood fill for O(1) unreachable checks, and a per-AI-call path cache.

findings.title: Theme-pack textures were cached globally and never unloaded
findings.evidence: Textures were cached by data-URL key with no Assets.unload call — browsing theme packs accumulated GPU memory until a full reload.
findings.impact: Extended sessions involving theme browsing could degrade or crash on memory-constrained devices.
findings.fix: unloadThemeTextures() added and called from MapCanvas cleanup / pack-switch.

findings.title: Between-turns ad slot remounted and re-injected its script every AI turn
findings.evidence: The ad component remounted on every AI turn, re-injecting the third-party ad network's script tag each time — a real policy-violation risk with production ad networks.
findings.impact: Repeated script re-injection wastes bandwidth/CPU and risks violating ad-network terms of service.
findings.fix: Module-level script-injection guard (claimScriptInjection/hasScriptFailed) ensures the ad script loads once per page.

findings.title: 18 MB of binaries in plain git, including uncompressed WAV music
findings.evidence: Three ~1.75MB WAV music loops were served verbatim (OGG/M4A would be roughly 10x smaller); no asset-size budget existed in CI; every art-regeneration pass permanently grew git history.
findings.impact: Mobile players downloaded 5+ MB of music that could be ~500KB; clone size grows monotonically with every asset-regeneration round.
findings.fix: PARTIAL: music now ships as OGG+M4A with a CI asset-size budget guard (300KB static-asset ceiling). NOT done (operator-flagged, still open): the original uncommitted-removal of the legacy WAV files and adoption of git-LFS for art/audio history.

findings.title: AI combat-tactic thresholds were hardcoded in the engine
findings.evidence: Flee/board thresholds and the unit-ranking formula lived in the engine instead of @aop/content, violating the project's own engine/content separation and making them untunable via the balance-sim tooling.
findings.impact: AI combat tuning could not be adjusted or A/B-tested without an engine code change and redeploy.
findings.fix: Thresholds lifted into TacticsTuning/AiCombatTuning in @aop/content, injected via the frozen match config, following the established content-injection pattern.

findings.title: GameState had no schema-version field
findings.evidence: Compatibility rested entirely on optional-field sniffing — the first non-additive engine change would make old snapshots replay to silently different states, undetectable and unfixable retroactively post-launch.
findings.impact: A future engine change could corrupt historical replays with no way to detect or repair it after the fact.
findings.fix: rulesVersion added to GameConfig, stamped by createGame and asserted on replay/applyAction, throwing RulesVersionMismatchError on mismatch.

findings.title: Dead faction parameter threaded through captainToCombatant
findings.evidence: A no-op faction parameter plus two unnecessary non-null-assert lookups gave a misleading impression that faction affects combat conversion when it didn't.
findings.impact: Minor — a maintenance/readability tax and a latent null-assert risk with no functional consequence.
findings.fix: Parameter and the associated lookups removed from captainToCombatant's signature.

findings.title: Replay/adversarial test coverage gap for the anti-cheat boundary
findings.status: Reviewed — no issue filed (clean scan result)
findings.evidence: No adversarial-payload tests (NaN/0.5/-1/Infinity) or validator/createGame consistency tests existed — all three concrete engine holes above (F-01, F-02, F-22) would have been caught by this coverage. Folded into the #205/#206 fix PRs rather than filed as its own issue.
findings.impact: The anti-cheat boundary shipped without tests for the exact failure modes that turned out to be real, exploitable holes.
findings.fix: Adversarial suite added: per-field NaN/0.5/-1/Infinity rejection tests, a validated-map-to-createGame property test, and a resign-then-interact replay-log test.

findings.title: createQuickMatch duplicated the start-match pipeline
findings.evidence: displayNames-join logic was hand-reimplemented four times (start-match, matchmaking, get-leaderboard, browse-maps), and createQuickMatch duplicated the whole start-match pipeline.
findings.impact: Any bugfix or behavior change to match-start or display-name resolution had to be applied in up to four places, and reliably wasn't.
findings.fix: displayNames() and startMatch() extracted into shared helpers used by all four call sites.

findings.title: Edge functions had zero CI coverage
findings.evidence: CI ran only pnpm-workspace typecheck/test/build; supabase/functions isn't a pnpm workspace and had no tsconfig — Deno tests plausibly never executed anywhere. This is the most security-sensitive code in the repo (anti-cheat boundary, Stripe webhook, turn pipeline).
findings.impact: A type error or contract break in any edge function — including the anti-cheat boundary — could merge green with zero verification.
findings.fix: New edge-functions CI job runs deno check over every supabase/functions/*/index.ts plus deno test with the deno.json import map.

findings.title: No deploy pipeline for any tier
findings.evidence: Migrations were validated locally but never pushed; functions were documented as manually deployed; nothing smoke-tested a deployed stack. A forgotten function deploy after an engine/shared change risked a client-vs-server version desync.
findings.impact: Go-live required a human to hand-deploy three independently versioned tiers in the correct order with no automated check.
findings.fix: Deploy workflow added: supabase db push -> functions deploy -> Vercel deploy from one commit, plus smoke tests; deliberately workflow_dispatch-only pending a real production project.

findings.title: buildMatchConfig/buildCatalog were duplicated client/server and had already drifted
findings.evidence: Two hand-maintained 'byte-for-byte identical' copies had already diverged — the client catalog included resourceNodes, the server twin omitted it, undetected because the field was optional and edge functions weren't typechecked in CI.
findings.impact: Once community maps with resource nodes became playable in multiplayer, server-run matches would silently yield different income than the client's optimistic simulation — broken replays with no error.
findings.fix: A golden parity test (catalogParity.test.ts) now deep-equals buildCatalog/buildMatchConfig output from both runtimes on every CI run; resourceNodes drift is closed.

findings.title: ENGINE_VERSION was a never-bumped constant that couldn't cover content changes
findings.evidence: The constant hadn't moved since repo creation despite repeated engine behavior changes; worse, replay rebuilt GameConfig from the currently-bundled content, so a pure balance change could silently alter old replays with the version guard still passing.
findings.impact: Post-launch, any engine or content-balance deploy could invalidate in-flight/finished match replays with no detection.
findings.fix: ENGINE_VERSION replaced with a generated content hash (engineVersion.generated.ts) covering engine + content inputs, with a CI test failing if it goes stale.

findings.title: No error reporting or alerting in any tier
findings.evidence: No client error-reporting SDK, no ErrorBoundary (prior to F-31's fix) or global handlers; server errors collapsed into short-retention logs; nothing read cron.job_run_details. First detection of any production breakage was always a user complaint.
findings.impact: A bad deploy, a stalled cron, or a webhook failure at go-live would be invisible until a user reported it.
findings.fix: Sentry wired client-side (with ErrorBoundary) and server-side (@sentry/deno in the shared error path); a 15-minute synthetic-monitor GitHub Action probes functions and cron heartbeats.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md described a stack that doesn't exist
findings.evidence: Claimed zod schemas (none exist — hand-rolled guards by design), Zustand state (none — hand-rolled context/reducers), four factions (five ship, French included), and a stale/incomplete function list.
findings.impact: The doc CLAUDE.md points agents and reviewers at as ground truth was actively wrong, seeding incorrect assumptions in every future review or agent session.
findings.fix: Doc corrected: five-faction list, actual validation/state approach described, function list points at the functions README, packages/tools added, phantom env-var claim removed.

findings.title: @aop/shared had no test runner of its own
findings.evidence: Load-bearing logic (map-code decoder with decode-bomb hardening, pagination cursors, matchmaking grouping, rating math) was tested only incidentally from other packages' suites — pnpm --filter @aop/shared test ran nothing.
findings.impact: Shared-only changes couldn't be verified in isolation, and coverage could be silently deleted by anyone trimming an unrelated package's tests.
findings.fix: vitest + a test script added to packages/shared; the shared-logic test files moved next to the code they verify.

findings.title: Shared TS constants and immutable SQL check constraints had no parity guard
findings.evidence: MAX_CHAT_LENGTH and three other limits were literally duplicated into SQL CHECK constraints in already-applied (immutable) migrations, with nothing enforcing they stay in sync.
findings.impact: Raising a limit in TS alone would ship green, then every request past the old SQL limit would surface as a raw constraint-violation 500 instead of a friendly validation error.
findings.fix: constants-parity.test.ts reads the migration files as text and asserts each TS constant's value appears in the current constraint definition; verified passing for all four constants.

findings.title: New-game setup offered unplayable hotseat multi-human seats
findings.evidence: GameScreen's viewer was permanently anchored to the first human seat — a second human seat got ignored taps, a locked City screen, and wrong fog, with only End Turn/Resign functional.
findings.impact: A player configuring a hotseat game would produce an effectively broken match for every seat after the first.
findings.fix: The multi-human toggle removed from setup — seats 1+ are always AI until real hotseat (pass-device) support is built.

findings.title: World map surface was pointer-only with no accessibility path
findings.evidence: No keyboard or assistive-tech path existed to the core game surface; the canvas was unlabeled and QuickMatch displayed raw faction IDs instead of names.
findings.impact: The core gameplay surface was entirely unusable for keyboard-only or assistive-technology users.
findings.fix: role="application" plus tile-cursor keyboard navigation and an aria-live status region added to MapCanvas; QuickMatch now renders faction display names.

findings.title: Community map import/download replaced the working draft with no confirmation
findings.status: Reviewed — no issue filed (clean scan result)
findings.evidence: Download and Import Code both silently replaced the in-progress editor draft; only New Blank Map had a confirmation, making the three destructive paths inconsistent. Tracked within the #238 map-editor-draft issue's range rather than its own distinct issue number.
findings.impact: A map author could lose in-progress work to an inconsistently-guarded import action.
findings.fix: All three destructive paths (New/Generate/Import) now route through the same guardedReplace() confirmation helper.

findings.title: PII/data-classification scan — no true PII columns found
findings.status: Reviewed — no issue filed (clean scan result)
findings.evidence: Static scan (tools/pii-classify.mjs) of all 23 migration files against 91 columns across 15 tables (live DB was unmigrated/empty at scan time, so this is a schema-level scan, not a live-data scan). 3 columns matched the ambiguous 'NAME?' low-confidence rule; zero columns matched any high/medium-confidence PII, PHI, or PCI pattern (no email/SSN/DOB/phone/address/payment fields in the schema).
findings.impact: Clean result for a game backend — the only ambiguous matches are display-name-shaped fields, correctly flagged low-confidence rather than asserted as PII, and none require special handling beyond normal auth-adjacent data care.
findings.fix: No action required. Re-run against the live database once it's migrated, to confirm no PII was introduced via runtime-only columns not present in migration SQL.
